parsed.explanation: No traveler-facing restriction is documented: entry, documents, facilities, custody and police interaction show no trans-specific exposure. Protections exist — the 2008 Anti-Discrimination Act covers gender identity in goods and services, and institutions demonstrably function (bills failed, referendum question struck down). But the climate is hostile and volatile: a lethal 2022 shooting at a capital LGBT bar, an attacked first Pride, recurring far-right bills to criminalise transition (failed), a 2024 in-government hostile statement, hate-crime law excluding gender identity, unstable trans-care standards, and falling public support. Severity-if-outed is mostly social discrimination with paper recourse, not state targeting; the lethal incident is singular, not a pattern. This sits above universal-friction dossiers (~0.55) and below tolerance-with-working-enforcement tiers (~0.75–0.85).

entry_documents.exposure: No entry or documentation obstacle specific to a trans visitor; free-movement rules apply.
entry_documents.protection: Regional-union free movement; no marker-examination or mismatch screening documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor documents come from home country; domestic LGR restrictions do not reach visitors.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented arrest, detention or custody-placement exposure for trans visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Criminalisation bills failed; no enforced statute against gender expression documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facility-access restriction (bathrooms, wards, shelters) documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Anti-Discrimination Act (2004/2008) covers gender identity in goods and services — an operative traveler-facing protection on paper.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Enforcement in practice is not documented as tested.

care_services.exposure: Standards of care revoked May 2022, providers refusing trans care by Nov 2022; republished March 2023 but implementation unresolved — a visitor seeking care risks refusal or instability.
care_services.interaction: Care-seeking could expose a visitor to providers; outcome uncertain.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Recurring far-right bills to ban gender change and criminalise transition (prison ≥4 years in 2023 draft); culture minister's 2024 hostile statement; karyotype bill passed first reading with 87 votes.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: All bills failed; anti-discrimination law retained.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Failed legislation signals legislative threat-framing but no enacted traveler-facing rule.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented for traveling minors; referendum-era proposals on school sex education failed.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Lethal 2022 shooting at a capital LGBT bar (two killed, attacker also died); 2010 Pride attacked with stones and tear gas; hostile, volatile public opinion.
street_violence_police_response.protection: 29 arrests at 2010 Pride; constitution applied to strike referendum question — institutions act, but no documented hate-crime recourse for gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Hate-crime statute covers sexual orientation only; trans victims face a documented gap.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Open questions: whether republished standards reach clinics and registries; fate of the 24 Feb 2023 bill; actual enforcement of anti-discrimination protections for visitors.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning legislature and courts documented as restraining hostile proposals.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Thin-data gaps resolve toward the documented structural hostility, not neutrality.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.65-A documents a documented police stop with intrusive questioning and biased enforcement, offset by working courts. This dossier documents no traveler-specific police exposure at all, but its climate (lethal venue attack, ministerial hostility, failed criminalisation bills) is harsher; net position is comparable, around 0.64.

0.75-D has nightlife assaults with prosecution when evidence is clear and an operating review board. This dossier has one lethal venue attack, no documented GI hate-crime coverage, and unstable care access — measurably below the 0.75 band.

0.55-E features systemic selective scrutiny and ejection by transit police — a recurring traveler-facing exposure. This dossier shows no comparable systematic traveler friction; its worst features are dated incidents and hostile climate with intact institutions, so it sits above 0.55.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime poses no structural barrier to a trans visitor: entry is unobstructed, no facility or custody rule targets trans people, and gender identity is covered by anti-discrimination law in goods and services. The operative exposures are climate-driven: a volatile and regionally hostile public opinion, one lethal and one historical attack on LGBT venues concentrated in the capital, unstable trans-care standards that could refuse a care-seeking visitor, hate-crime law omitting gender identity, and a legislature repeatedly entertaining criminalisation of transition — though each bill failed and courts have restrained hostile measures. Severity-if-outed is chiefly discrimination and social hostility with paper recourse, not state enforcement; single lethal incidents carry limited statistical weight in a medium country but, combined with ministerial hostility and unresolved care access, hold the rating in the upper Reduced Risk range rather than Low Risk.
